駅 · えき · Train and bus stations. For the first two of either of those, use the wago counting method: 一駅 is ひとえき, 二駅 is ふたえき. After that, use the kango.
あと １[いち]月[がつ]で お正月[しょうがつ]だね。
It will be the New Year in one month.

月 · つき/がつ · Months. 月 is a counter used to count the number of months ("10 months" is １０ヶ月) as well as identify the calendar month ("October" is １０月). Depending on what you're counting or how it's used, the way it gets read (つき vs げつ vs がつ) changes, so be aware of that.
３[さん]校[こう] 合同[ごうどう]で 遠足[えんそく]に 行[い]った。
Three schools went on a school trip together.
校 · こう · Schools, proofreading (校正) corrections.
１[いち]度[ど] ２人[ふたり]で 話[はなし]を しませんか？
Why don't we have a talk once, just the two of us?

度 · ど/たび · The number of times something happens, chances, opportunities, experiences, series of actions, divided actions, degrees, temperature, etc. Depending on what you use it for, 度 can be read as either ど or たび. The numbering system can either be wago or kango, depending on the number and what you're counting: it's kango for ど and wago for たび, but たび is only used to count up to the number three in modern Japanese.
コートを ４[よん]着[ちゃく] 持[も]っています。
着 · ちゃく · Clothes—one coat, ten skirts, etc. But, it is also the ordinal number suffix for first place, second place, etc., in a race. This is because the word 着く means "to arrive."
明日[あした]の ご飯[はん]の ことを 考[かんが]える。
１００[ひゃく]円[えん]しか 持[も]っていません。

I studied Japanese for three months.
箇月 · かげつ · Number of months. As in, "for three months" or "in three months." More often, you'll see the hiragana か or a small ヵ or ヶ instead of the kanji 箇.
ちょっと 1[いち]服[ふく] してから 行[い]くよ。
I'm gonna go after I have a quick smoke.
服 · ふく · Doses of medicine, poison, or drugs, sips of tea, doses, bowls of matcha, puffs or tokes of a cigarette, rest, etc.
世界[せかい]の ７[なな]海[かい]の 名前[なまえ]を 言[い]えますか?

前菜[ぜんさい]は ３[さん]品[ぴん] ご用意[ようい] しております。
We prepared three dishes for the appetizer.

品 · しな/ひん · 品 is used to count items, products, or dishes of food. In situations where it's pronounced しな, you'll want to use the wago counting method for one (一品/ひとしな) and two (二品/ふたしな). After that it's all kango. When pronounced as ひん, this counter just uses the kango counting method right from the start.
この 村[むら]には 図書[としょ]館[かん]が １[いち]館[かん]も ない。
There isn't even one library in this village!
館 · かん · This counts institutions ending with 館, such as art galleries or art museums (美術館), libraries (図書館), museums (博物館), or aquariums (水族館).
ペンを １[いっ]本[ぽん] 貸[か]してくれませんか？

ここに １[いち]ヶ所[かしょ] スペルミスが あるよ。
There is a typo right here.
箇所 · かしょ · Places, spots, points, passages, etc. Basically any kind of place. The kanji 箇 is often written with the hiragana か or a small ヵ or ヶ.
ベンは ベンツを ９[きゅう]台[だい] もっています。
Ben owns nine Mercedes Benz cars.
台 · だい · Platforms you can stand or put things on, machines, cars, large instruments, and more.
今[いま]までに 仕上[しあ]げた 作品[さくひん]は ３[さん]作[さく]です。
So far, I've made three works of art.

もう ３[さん]歩[ぽ]ほど 後[うし]ろに 下[さ]がってもらえますか？

歩 · ほ · Steps. This can refer to both physical steps while you're walking as well as less physical steps of progress in a project, etc.
ここから 日本[にほん]への フライトは １[いち]日[にち] １[いち] 便[びん]しか ない。
There is only one flight per day from here to Japan.

便 · びん · 便 is used to count the number of flights, boats shipping out, long-distance buses, etc. over a period of time. It can also be used as an ordinal number suffix for delivery or transportation. If you're referring to a flight number, for example, you could use this ordinal number suffix.
